name: Marcus
summary: Trade contractor running two kitchen-and-bath crews in the Dallas suburbs; buys cabinetry repeatedly and is judged by his clients on call-backs.
description: Kitchen and bath remodeling contractor, 12 years in, two crews, a dispatcher and a phone that rings on ladders. Buys doors and boxes from three shops and drops the one that costs him a call-back.
lifestyle: On site by 6:30, quotes at the kitchen table after nine, Saturdays for walk-throughs.
aspirations: A referral-only book of business with no call-back week on the calendar.
typical_quote: I do not need it pretty on day one. I need it to look the same at month eighteen.
background_story: Started as a finish carpenter, went out on his own in 2014, added a second crew in 2022. Lost a repeat client in 2025 over a lacquer failure that was the cabinet shop's fault and his invoice.
primary_goals: Zero call-backs in the first year
A cabinet shop that hits the install date
Finishes that survive a working kitchen
motivations: A crew that is never waiting on doors
pain_points: A finish that lifts inside a year and lands on his invoice
Lead times that slip after the demo is booked
Shop drawings that miss the false fronts
challenges: Explaining a shop's failure to his own client
Keeping two crews fed with work
frustrations: Shops that promise a date and go quiet
Being told the finish failure was the homeowner's cleaning products
content_preferences: Case studies with the mistake left in
Anything a foreman can read in a truck

buying_behavior.trigger: A call-back on a finish or a slipped install date on the current job
buying_behavior.decision_cycle: One job to trial a shop, then a standing order if the first year is clean
stakeholders: The homeowner on the affected job
buying_behavior.preferred_intake: A shop walk-through and one reference job he can drive to
objections: Every shop says its finish lasts; mine have all failed at least once
A longer finish schedule means a longer lead time

online_behavior.content_habits: Reads LinkedIn at 6am and Facebook trade groups after nine; saves process posts, never comments on hype
